title.zh: 卷365 列傳一百五十二 觉罗宝兴 宗室敬徴 宗室禧恩 陈官俊 卓秉恬
title.en: Volume 365 Biographies 152: Jue Luo Bao Xing, Zong Shijingzheng, Zong Shixien, Chen Guanjun, Zhuo Bingtian
title.raw: 卷365 列傳一百五十二 觉罗宝兴 宗室敬徴 宗室禧恩 陈官俊 卓秉恬

sentences.zh: 列傳一百五十二

translations.literal: Biographies 152
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 152

sentences.zh: 覺羅寶興宗室敬徵宗室禧恩陳官俊卓秉恬

translations.literal: Jueluo Baoxing, Zongshi Jingzheng, Zongshi Xi'en, Chen Guanjun, Zhuo Bingtian
translations.idiomatic: Jueluo Baoxing, Zongshi Jingzheng, Zongshi Xi'en, Chen Guanjun, and Zhuo Bingtian

sentences.zh: 覺羅寶興，字獻山，隸鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: Jueluo Baoxing, style name Xianshan, was registered in the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Jueluo Baoxing, whose style name was Xianshan, belonged to the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the civil examinations as a jinshi in the fifteenth year of the Jiaqing reign (1810), entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷少詹事，入直上書房。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Junior Chamberlain for Ceremonials and entered service in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Junior Chamberlain for Ceremonials and joined the staff of the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 十八年，仁宗幸熱河，林清逆黨突入禁城，寶興散直，至東華門與賊遇，急入告警。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Emperor Renzong went to Rehe; Lin Qing's rebel faction suddenly entered the Forbidden City. Baoxing had finished his duty rotation, reached the Donghua Gate and encountered bandits, and hurried inside to give the alarm.
translations.idiomatic: In 1813, while Emperor Jiaqing was at Rehe, rebels loyal to Lin Qing stormed the Forbidden City. Baoxing was off duty when he reached the Donghua Gate, met the attackers, and rushed inside to raise the alarm.

sentences.zh: 宣宗方在上書房，聞警戒備，賊不得逞。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was then in the Upper Study; hearing the alarm he put the guard on alert, and the bandits could not act out their plans.
translations.idiomatic: The future Daoguang Emperor was in the Upper Study; hearing the alarm, he ordered the guards to stand ready, and the rebels were unable to carry out their plot.

sentences.zh: 上還京，擢寶興內閣學士。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned to the capital, Baoxing was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to Beijing, Baoxing was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1814 he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以事忤旨，詔斥寶興不學，降大理寺卿，罷直書房。

translations.literal: Because of a matter that offended the imperial will, an edict rebuked Baoxing for being unlearned, demoted him to President of the Court of Judicial Review, and removed him from duty in the Study.
translations.idiomatic: After he gave offence on a matter of policy, an edict denounced Baoxing as unlearned, demoted him to President of the Court of Judicial Review, and stripped him of his posting in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 复坐部刊科場條例誤「高宗」為「高祖」，降二級調用。

translations.literal: Again, because in publishing examination regulations his ministry mistakenly wrote "Gaozong" for "Gaozu," he was demoted two ranks and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: He was later punished again when his ministry's published examination regulations mistook "Gaozong" for "Gaozu," and he was demoted two ranks and reassigned.

sentences.zh: 尋予三等侍衛，充吐魯番領隊大臣。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was granted the rank of Third Class Bodyguard and appointed leader of the Turfan expedition.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the rank of third-class bodyguard and sent to Turfan as leader of the imperial detachment.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，召為大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he was recalled as Vice President of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he was recalled to serve as Vice President of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 復因事降通政司參議，歷左副都御史、兵部侍郎，出為泰宁鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Again because of affairs he was demoted to Counselor of the Office of Transmission, served successively as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War, and went out as Major General of Ta'ning Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted again on another charge to counselor in the Office of Transmission, then served as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War before being posted out as commander of the Ta'ning Garrison.

sentences.zh: 八年，授理籓院侍郎，調兵部。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In 1828 he was made Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and then transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 迭命偕戶部尚書王鼎察治長蘆、兩淮鹽務，籌議整頓，詳王鼎傳。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly ordered together with Wang Ding, Minister of Revenue, to investigate and rectify the Changlu and Lianghuai salt administrations and discuss plans for their overhaul; details are in Wang Ding's biography.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly ordered, together with Minister of Revenue Wang Ding, to investigate and reform the Changlu and Lianghuai salt monopolies; the account appears in Wang Ding's biography.

sentences.zh: 十年，出為吉林將軍，疏言：「松花江西岸、輝發河北岸舊例封禁，其餘閒曠山場均設卡倫，惟許兵丁打捕牲畜，以備貢品。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he went out as Military Governor of Jilin and memorialized, saying: "Along the west bank of the Songhua River and the north bank of the Huifa River there is the old rule of closed borders; in the rest of the idle mountain wastes guard posts are all established, only permitting soldiers to hunt and capture livestock to supply tribute items."
translations.idiomatic: In 1830 he was appointed Military Governor of Jilin. In a memorial he wrote that by long-standing regulation the west bank of the Songhua and the north bank of the Huifa River remained under seal, while elsewhere in the vacant hills guard posts were manned so that only troops might hunt game and livestock to fill tribute quotas.

sentences.zh: 民人無照，私出挖蓡斫木者，查拏治罪。

translations.literal: Civilians without permits who privately went out to dig ginseng or fell timber were to be searched out, arrested, and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Any civilian who left the zone without a permit to dig ginseng or cut timber was to be hunted down and punished.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「伯都訥珠爾山荒田先後開墾五千二百六十二晌，其租息請自道光十五年為始，以其半分賞兵丁，半存備報修工程。

translations.literal: He also said: "On the waste fields of Borderedun Zhuer Mountain, 5,262 shang have been opened for cultivation in succession; please have the rent and interest begin from the fifteenth year of Daoguang, using half to reward soldiers and half stored to prepare for reporting and repair projects."
translations.idiomatic: He further reported that 5,262 shang of wasteland on Borderedun Zhuer Mountain had been brought under the plough in stages. He asked that rent begin in 1835, with half distributed as rewards to troops and half set aside for maintenance and repairs.

sentences.zh: 此外尚有可墾荒地五萬六千餘晌，作為官荒，將來奏請招佃徵租。

translations.literal: Beyond this there is still cultivable wasteland of more than 56,000 shang, to be treated as official waste land; in future please memorialize to recruit tenants and collect rent.
translations.idiomatic: More than 56,000 additional shang of land could still be opened; he proposed reserving these as state wasteland and bringing tenants in under imperial lease later.

sentences.zh: 烏拉涼水泉已墾七萬三千九百餘晌，請撥二道河東二萬晌，以七成給烏拉總管衙門，三成給協領衙門，資為津貼。

translations.literal: At Wula Liangshuiquan, 73,900-odd shang have already been cultivated; please allot 20,000 shang east of Erdao River, giving 70 percent to the Wula Commandant's office and 30 percent to the Assistant Commandant's office as allowance funds.
translations.idiomatic: At Wula Liangshuiquan more than 73,900 shang had already been reclaimed. He requested assigning 20,000 shang east of Erdao River, with seventy percent going to the Wula commandant's yamen and thirty percent to the assistant commandant's yamen as supplementary income.

sentences.zh: 餘未墾地五萬三千餘晌，亦作官荒。

translations.literal: The remaining uncultivated land of 53,000-odd shang is also to be treated as official waste land.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining 53,000-odd shang of unreclaimed land should likewise be kept as state wasteland.

sentences.zh: 」並從之。

translations.literal: The memorial was all approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved these proposals in full.

sentences.zh: 調盛京，又調成都。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Shengjing, then again to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Shengjing, then again to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 十七年，署四川總督，逾年實授。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he served as Acting Governor-General of Sichuan; the following year he received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1837 he served as acting Governor-General of Sichuan and received the substantive post the year after.

sentences.zh: 時馬邊、越巂邊外夷匪數出為患。

translations.literal: At that time beyond the borders of Mabian and Yuexi, Yi bandits frequently came out and caused trouble.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yi raiders beyond the Mabian and Yuexi frontiers were making repeated incursions.

sentences.zh: 十九年，疏言：「禦邊之策，不外剿、撫、防三者，撫之之道，在施於平時，斷無失利之後轉而就撫之理。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he memorialized, saying: "Strategies for defending the frontier are nothing beyond suppression, pacification, and defense. The way of pacification lies in applying it in normal times; there is absolutely no principle of turning to pacification after suffering defeat."
translations.idiomatic: In 1839 he memorialized that frontier policy amounted to suppression, pacification, and defense—and that pacification had to be pursued in peacetime, not adopted only after military setbacks.

sentences.zh: 比來勞師糜餉，迄無成功。

translations.literal: Recently troops have been exhausted and supplies wasted, yet there has been no success to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Recent campaigns had exhausted the troops and drained the treasury without achieving a lasting result.

sentences.zh: 為今計者，以修邊防為急務，陳防邊五事：一、增兵額，請於馬邊增兵千二百，雷波、普安、安阜、越巂、寧越各增兵八百，瓘邊、屏山各增兵四百；

translations.literal: For the present plan, strengthening frontier defense is the urgent task. He set forth five matters for defending the border: First, increase troop quotas—request at Mabian an increase of 1,200 troops, at Leibo, Pu'an, Anfu, Yuexi, and Ningyue each 800, and at Qianbian and Pingshan each 400;
translations.idiomatic: What was needed now, he argued, was to strengthen the frontier defenses. He proposed five measures: first, increase troop strength—1,200 more at Mabian, 800 each at Leibo, Pu'an, Anfu, Yuexi, and Ningyue, and 400 each at Qianbian and Pingshan;

sentences.zh: 一、改營製，請以綏定協副將移駐馬邊廳城，游擊、都司以下各增設移駐有差；

translations.literal: Second, reform the garrison system—request that the Suiding Brigade Deputy Commander move his headquarters to Mabian subprefecture city, with brigade commanders, battalion commanders, and below each increased and relocated in varying degrees;
translations.idiomatic: second, reorganize the garrison system by moving the Suiding Brigade deputy commander to Mabian city and redeploying brigade, battalion, and company officers as required;

sentences.zh: 一、築碉堡，飭各廳縣因地制宜，多修堡寨，責令各集團練，官給抬砲，督率教演，擇要隘築砲台，增設大砲；

translations.literal: Third, build blockhouses and forts—order each subprefecture and county according to local conditions to build many forts and stockades, charge each community militia group to drill, supply swivel guns from the government, supervise and lead training exercises, select strategic passes to build gun platforms, and add large cannon;
translations.idiomatic: third, build blockhouses and stockades across the subprefectures and counties, organize local militia, issue swivel guns, drill the men, and erect gun platforms with heavy artillery at key passes;

sentences.zh: 一、定期巡閱，歲春夏之交，建昌道赴越巂、瓘邊，永寧道赴馬邊、雷波、屏山，週曆巡閱各一次，秋冬責成提督與建昌總兵分赴巡行察勘邊隘；

translations.literal: Fourth, conduct regular inspections—between spring and summer each year the Jianchang Circuit Intendant goes to Yuexi and Qianbian, the Yongning Circuit Intendant goes to Mabian, Leibo, and Pingshan, each making a full circuit inspection once; in autumn and winter charge the Provincial Commander-in-Chief and Jianchang Major General each to go on inspection tours to examine frontier passes;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, institute regular inspections—the Jianchang circuit intendant to tour Yuexi and Qianbian each spring, the Yongning circuit intendant to tour Mabian, Leibo, and Pingshan, and in autumn the provincial commander and Jianchang major general to inspect the border passes;

sentences.zh: 一、優獎邊吏，馬邊、越巂兩廳同知，請三年俸滿，以題調選缺知府升補。

translations.literal: Fifth, reward frontier officials favorably—the subprefectural magistrates of Mabian and Yuexi, please after three years when salary term is complete promote them by title-selection to fill prefectural magistrate vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: fifth, reward frontier officials—the Mabian and Yuexi subprefects to be promoted to prefect after three years of service on the border.

sentences.zh: 」疏下議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred for deliberation and approved for implementation.

sentences.zh: 言官論奏四川提督應如湖南例，半年駐越巂等處。

translations.literal: Censorial officials memorialized in discussion that the Sichuan Provincial Commander-in-Chief should follow the Hunan precedent and reside half the year at Yuexi and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists argued that the Sichuan provincial commander should follow the Hunan precedent and spend half the year stationed at Yuexi and neighboring posts.

sentences.zh: 寶興議：「馬邊、越巂相距遼遠，請於春秋夷匪出沒之時，提督往駐馬邊、瓘邊、雷波三廳，建昌總兵往駐越巂、寧越。

translations.literal: Baoxing deliberated: "Mabian and Yuexi are far apart; please in spring and autumn when Yi bandits appear and disappear, have the Provincial Commander-in-Chief go to garrison the three subprefectures of Mabian, Qianbian, and Leibo, and the Jianchang Major General go to garrison Yuexi and Ningyue."
translations.idiomatic: Baoxing countered that Mabian and Yuexi were too far apart for one commander to cover both. He proposed that in spring and autumn, when raiders were most active, the provincial commander should station himself at Mabian, Qianbian, and Leibo while the Jianchang major general took Yuexi and Ningyue.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「越巂邊防以大路為重，麥子營、利濟站均應增駐弁兵，乾溝諸汛應酌量移撤，分設於馬日槓諸處。

translations.literal: He also said: "For Yuexi frontier defense the main road is crucial; Maiziying and Lijizhan both should have increased garrison of officers and troops. The guard posts at Qiangou and elsewhere should be weighed for relocation and withdrawal, and distributed to places such as Marigang."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged strengthening the main road defenses at Maiziying and Lijizhan, and redeploying troops from minor posts such as Qiangou to strategic points including Marigang.

sentences.zh: 越巂、寧越兩營相距頗遠，聲勢不能相及。

translations.literal: The two battalions of Yuexi and Ningyue are quite far apart, and their combined force cannot reach each other.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuexi and Ningyue battalions were too widely separated to support one another.

sentences.zh: 前請以建昌左營游擊移駐大菩薩地，遠在寧越之東，而越巂營參將復與游擊不相統屬。

translations.literal: Previously it was requested that the Jianchang Left Battalion brigade commander move his headquarters to Dapusa, far to the east of Ningyue, while the Yuexi Battalion colonel again is not in the command hierarchy of the brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: An earlier proposal to move the Jianchang Left Battalion brigade commander to Dapusa would have placed him far east of Ningyue, yet he would not have fallen under the Yuexi battalion colonel's command.

sentences.zh: 請越巂、寧越適中之界牌樓，以建昌鎮右營都司移駐，專管麥子營、利濟站兩汛。

translations.literal: Please at Jiepailou, the midpoint between Yuexi and Ningyue, have the Jianchang Garrison Right Battalion company commander move his headquarters, exclusively managing the two guard posts of Maiziying and Lijizhan.
translations.idiomatic: He asked instead that the Jianchang Garrison Right Battalion company commander be posted at Jiepailou, midway between Yuexi and Ningyue, with sole responsibility for Maiziying and Lijizhan.

sentences.zh: 」並從之。

translations.literal: These proposals were all approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved these arrangements as well.

sentences.zh: 先是寶興以馬邊諸廳縣增設防兵，籌議邊防經費，請按糧津貼，計可徵銀百萬兩，以三十萬為初設防兵之需。

translations.literal: Earlier Baoxing, because of increasing frontier defense troops in the Mabian subprefectures and counties, discussed frontier defense funds and requested levying grain subsidies, calculating that one million taels of silver could be collected, using 300,000 for the initial needs of establishing defense troops.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, to fund the new garrisons in the Mabian region, Baoxing had proposed a grain surcharge expected to yield one million taels, thirty thousand of which would cover the initial troop deployments.

sentences.zh: 每歲經費，即以餘銀七十萬兩生息，置田供支。

translations.literal: Annual expenses would use the remaining 700,000 taels of silver to generate interest and purchase land for support.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining seven hundred thousand taels would be invested for interest and used to purchase land whose rents would meet the annual upkeep.

sentences.zh: 上以津貼病民，撥部帑銀百萬。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered the subsidies harmful to the people and allocated one million taels from the ministry treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected the surcharge as a burden on the people and allocated one million taels from the central treasury instead.

sentences.zh: 翰林院侍讀學士王炳瀛奏：「四川前買義田，遍​​及百餘州縣，若更以數十萬帑銀於各州縣買田收租，膏腴將盡歸公產。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academy Reader Wang Bingying memorialized: "Sichuan previously purchased charity fields, spreading through more than a hundred prefectures and counties. If further using several hundred thousand taels of treasury silver to buy fields and collect rent in each prefecture and county, fertile land will all become public property."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Reader Wang Bingying objected that Sichuan already held charity fields across more than a hundred jurisdictions; spending hundreds of thousands of taels more to buy land for rent would concentrate the province's best farmland in government hands.

sentences.zh: 請限於四廳近邊地收買，安置屯防。

translations.literal: Please limit purchases to land near the four subprefectures on the frontier and establish garrison colonies for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He urged limiting purchases to land near the four frontier subprefectures and using it to settle garrison colonists.

sentences.zh: 」下寶興妥議，疏言：「邊防完竣，用銀二十二萬兩有奇，以三十七萬發鹽茶各商，歲得息三萬七千餘兩，足敷增設練勇餉械之需。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to Baoxing for proper deliberation. He memorialized: "Frontier defense completed will use a little more than 220,000 taels of silver. Lending 370,000 to salt and tea merchants, annual interest of a little more than 37,000 taels is sufficient to cover the needs for pay and weapons of the added trained braves."
translations.idiomatic: Baoxing was ordered to revise the plan. He reported that completing the frontier works would cost just over 220,000 taels; lending 370,000 to the salt and tea merchants would yield more than 37,000 taels a year in interest, enough to pay the new militia.

sentences.zh: 餘銀四十萬，聽部撥別用。

translations.literal: The remaining 400,000 taels of silver, let the ministry allocate for other uses.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining four hundred thousand taels could be reallocated by the ministry for other purposes.

sentences.zh: 」遂罷買田議，二十一年，拜文淵閣大學士，留四川總督任。

translations.literal: The plan to buy fields was then abandoned. In the twenty-first year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion while retaining his post as Governor-General of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The land-purchase scheme was dropped. In 1841 he was made Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion while remaining Governor-General of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時大學士琦善、協辦大學士伊里布相繼罷，在朝滿洲大臣鮮當上意，故有是授。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Secretary Qishan and Associate Grand Secretary Yilibu were dismissed in succession; Manchu ministers at court rarely pleased the Emperor's intent, and therefore there was this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Qishan and Associate Grand Secretary Yilibu had recently been dismissed, and few Manchu ministers at court enjoyed the emperor's confidence—circumstances that explain this appointment.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，入覲，命留京管理刑部，充上書房總師傅，兼翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he came to audience, was ordered to remain in the capital to manage the Ministry of Justice, appointed Chief Tutor of the Upper Study, and concurrently Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1846 he came to court, was ordered to remain in Beijing to head the Ministry of Justice, and was appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study and chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十八年元旦，加恩年老諸臣，加太保。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the twenty-eighth year, favor was extended to elderly ministers, and he was given the rank of Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of 1848, as part of a grace for elderly ministers, he was promoted to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 十月，卒，年七十二，諡文莊。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he died, age seventy-two; posthumous title Wenzuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month at the age of seventy-two and was given the posthumous title Wenzuang.

sentences.zh: 宗室敬徵，隸鑲白旗，肅親王永錫子。

translations.literal: Zongshi Jingzheng was registered in the Bordered White Banner, son of Prince Su Yongxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zongshi Jingzheng belonged to the Bordered White Banner and was a son of Prince Su Yongxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年，封輔國公，授頭等侍衛，兼委散秩大臣、副都統。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing he was enfeoffed as Duke Who Assists the State, appointed First Class Bodyguard, and concurrently entrusted as Minister Without Portfolio and Vice Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1805 he was enfeoffed as Duke Who Assists the State, appointed a first-class bodyguard, and concurrently served as minister without portfolio and vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授內閣學士，兼鑾儀使，充總族長。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, concurrently Director of Imperial Processions, and served as Chief of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1814 he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, made concurrent director of imperial processions, and named chief of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，失察宗室海康等習紅陽教，褫職，謫居盛京。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, for failure to detect that clansmen Haikang and others practiced the Hongyang sect, he was stripped of office and banished to reside in Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1817 he was dismissed for failing to detect that clansmen including Haikang had joined the Hongyang sect, and was banished to Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 尋予四等侍衛，乾清門行走。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was granted Fourth Class Bodyguard and allowed to attend at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as a fourth-class bodyguard with attendance at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.

sentences.zh: 道光初，累遷工部侍郎，授內務府大臣，調戶部。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daoguang he was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Works, appointed Minister of the Imperial Household, and transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daoguang reign he rose to Vice Minister of Works, was appointed minister of the Imperial Household, and was then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 八年，偕尚書王鼎察治長蘆鹽務，奏定歸補帑課章程，詳王鼎傳。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, together with Minister Wang Ding he investigated and rectified the Changlu salt administration, memorialized and fixed regulations for restoring treasury salt revenues; details are in Wang Ding's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In 1828 he joined Minister Wang Ding in reforming the Changlu salt monopoly and establishing rules for restoring treasury revenues; see Wang Ding's biography.

sentences.zh: 十二年，南河奸民陳堂等盜決於家灣官堤，命偕尚書硃士彥往勘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, ruffians of the Southern Rivers Chen Tang and others illicitly breached the official dike at Yujiawan; he was ordered together with Minister Zhu Shiyan to go investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1832, after ruffians led by Chen Tang illicitly breached the official dike at Yujiawan on the Southern Rivers, he was ordered to investigate together with Minister Zhu Shiyan.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「諸口已合，壩下尚未閉氣，間有蟄陷。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "The various breaches have been closed, but below the dam the seal has not yet taken, and there are occasional hidden collapses."
translations.idiomatic: He reported that although the breaches had been closed, the seal below the dam was not yet complete and hidden collapses still occurred.

sentences.zh: 陳堂等聽從逸犯陳端糾眾，以為從例問擬，疏防各官遣戍。

translations.literal: Chen Tang and others obeyed the escaped criminal Chen Duan in gathering a crowd; they were sentenced according to the precedent for accomplices. Officials negligent in defense were sent to frontier garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tang and his accomplices, who had followed the fugitive Chen Duan, were sentenced as accessories; negligent frontier officials were banished to garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 通判張懋祖賠修壩工不實，罰賠枷號。

translations.literal: Subprefect Zhang Maozu's compensation for repairing the dam works was not genuine; he was fined compensation and cangue.
translations.idiomatic: Subprefect Zhang Maozu was fined and placed in the cangue for failing to make good his promised contribution to the repair.

sentences.zh: 覆勘湖河各工，請擇要興修，高堰、山盱卑矮石工，分年改砌碎石；

translations.literal: On re-inspection of the various works on the lake and river routes, he requested selecting important ones for construction and repair; the low stone works at Gaoyan and Shanyu should be rebuilt with rubble stone over successive years;
translations.idiomatic: On re-inspection he recommended priority repairs, including rebuilding the low stone revetments at Gaoyan and Shanyu with rubble over several years;

sentences.zh: 信壩補還石工，智壩、仁河、義河壩改修石底；

translations.literal: restore the stone works at Xin Dam; at Zhi Dam, Ren River, and Yi River dams rebuild with stone foundations;
translations.idiomatic: restore the stone work at Xin Dam; and rebuild the foundations at Zhi Dam and the Ren and Yi River dams;

sentences.zh: 里河福興閘塌卸，急築；

translations.literal: the Fuxing Sluice on the Inner River has collapsed and must be urgently rebuilt;
translations.idiomatic: urgently rebuild the collapsed Fuxing Sluice on the Inner River;

sentences.zh: 揚河西岸加高磚工，改拋碎石。

translations.literal: raise the brick works on the west bank of the Yang River and change to casting rubble stone.
translations.idiomatic: raise the brick revetment on the west bank of the Yang River and replace it with rubble stone.

sentences.zh: 」並從之。

translations.literal: These proposals were all approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved these recommendations.

sentences.zh: 又會同兩江總督陶澍議定淮鹽票引兼行，言官所論官票運私、侵礙暢岸、爭佔馬頭三者皆可無慮，詔如原議行。

translations.literal: He also together with Liangjiang Governor-General Tao Zhu fixed regulations for the Lianghuai salt ticket and transport certificate to operate jointly. The three points censorial officials discussed—official tickets transporting private salt, encroaching on unimpeded banks, and competing for wharves—could all be disregarded without concern. An edict ordered implementation as originally proposed.
translations.idiomatic: He also worked with Liangjiang Governor-General Tao Zhu to implement joint salt tickets and transport permits for Lianghuai. Memorialists had warned of official tickets used for smuggling, encroachment on shipping lanes, and competition for wharves; Jingzheng argued these concerns were unfounded, and the throne ordered the original plan to proceed.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授左都御史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1834 he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 偕侍郎吳椿勘浙江海塘，疏言：「念裡亭至尖山柴工尚資禦溜，石塘仍當修整，鎮海及戴家橋汛議改竹簍，塊石不如條石坦水舊法為堅實。

translations.literal: Together with Vice Minister Wu Chun he investigated the Zhejiang seawall and memorialized, saying: "From Nianliting to Jianshan the fascine works still serve to resist the current; the stone seawall should still be repaired and put in order. At Zhenhai and Daijiaqiao guard posts it was proposed to change to bamboo crates; block stone is not as solid and firm as the old method of strip stone with level water."
translations.idiomatic: With Vice Minister Wu Chun he inspected the Zhejiang seawall and reported that fascine works from Nianliting to Jianshan still held against the tide and the stone seawall needed repair. Proposals to use bamboo crates at Zhenhai and Daijiaqiao were inferior to the older strip-stone revetment method.

sentences.zh: 烏龍廟以東，冬工暫緩。

translations.literal: East of Wulong Temple, winter works are temporarily deferred.
translations.idiomatic: Work east of Wulong Temple could be deferred until the next season.

sentences.zh: 」回京，擢兵部尚書，調工部。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital he was promoted to Minister of War and transferred to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to Beijing he was promoted to Minister of War and then transferred to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以孝穆皇后、孝慎皇后梓宮奉安龍泉峪，諏日不慎，罷尚書、都統，仍充內務府大臣。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, because in selecting the date for installing the coffins of Empress Xiaomu and Empress Xiaoshen at Longquan Valley he was not careful, he was dismissed as Minister and Commander-in-Chief but still served as Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he was dismissed as minister and commander-in-chief for carelessness in choosing the date for installing the coffins of Empresses Xiaomu and Xiaoshen at Longquan Valley, but retained his post in the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 十六年，署戶部侍郎，累遷工部尚書，兼都統。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he served as Acting Vice Minister of Revenue, was promoted in succession to Minister of Works, and concurrently Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1836 he served as acting Vice Minister of Revenue, rose to Minister of Works, and was made concurrent commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 東河總督栗毓美多用磚工，御史李蓴言其不便，命敬徵偕蓴往勘。

translations.literal: Eastern Rivers Governor-General Li Yumei used brick works extensively; Censor Li Chun said this was inconvenient, and Jingzheng was ordered together with Chun to go investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Rivers Governor-General Li Yumei favored brick revetments, Censor Li Chun objected, and Jingzheng was sent to investigate with him.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「已辦磚工尚屬整齊，輿論謂保灘護崖可資其力。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "The brick works already completed are still in good order; public opinion says protecting banks and cliffs can rely on their strength."
translations.idiomatic: He reported that existing brick works were still sound and that public opinion held they could protect banks and cliffs.

sentences.zh: 水深溜急之處，不及埽工鞏固，搶辦險工，未可深恃。

translations.literal: In places where water is deep and currents swift, they are not as secure as fascine works; for emergency repairs of dangerous works, they cannot be deeply relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Where water ran deep and fast, however, brick was less secure than fascine bundles and could not be relied on for emergency repairs.

sentences.zh: 請停止燒磚，改辦碎石。

translations.literal: Please stop firing bricks and change to providing rubble stone.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended halting brick production and using rubble stone instead.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 十八年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，南河揚河漫口，水由灌河入海。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the Yang River of the Southern Rivers overflowed its banks, and water entered the sea through the Guan River.
translations.idiomatic: In 1842 the Yang River on the Southern Rivers breached its banks, and the flood poured into the sea through the Guan River.

sentences.zh: 有議即改新河，河督麟慶以河流未定，遽難決議，命敬徵偕尚書廖鴻荃往勘。

translations.literal: Some proposed immediately changing to the new river course; River Commissioner Lin Qing, because the river course was not yet settled, found it difficult to decide hastily, and Jingzheng was ordered together with Minister Liao Hongquan to go investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Some officials urged an immediate shift to the new channel, but River Commissioner Lin Qing argued the course was still unsettled. Jingzheng was ordered to investigate with Minister Liao Hongquan.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「改河之議，在因勢利導。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "The proposal to change the river course lies in following the terrain and guiding advantageously."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that redirecting a river meant working with its natural tendencies.

sentences.zh: 今查灌河海口至蕭莊口門三百六十餘裡。

translations.literal: Now investigating from the Guan River estuary to Xiaozhuang mouth, more than 360 li.
translations.idiomatic: He found that from the Guan River estuary to the Xiaozhuang outlet measured more than 360 li.

sentences.zh: 新河正溜，由六塘出達灌口，其下游東北一百十里，滔滔直注。

translations.literal: The new river's main current, exiting through Liutang to reach the Guan mouth, for 110 li downstream to the northeast flows torrentially straight in.
translations.idiomatic: The new channel's main current ran from Liutang to the Guan mouth, then northeast for 110 li in a swift, direct flow.

sentences.zh: 惟當潮漲時，黃水相逼，壅閼不前，而上游自口門至響水口二百餘裡，支流忽分忽合，必須兩岸築堤束水，方免汎濫。

translations.literal: Only when the tide rises does the Yellow River water press upon it, blocking and obstructing forward flow; while upstream from the mouth to Xiangshui mouth, more than 200 li, branch streams suddenly divide and suddenly merge—dikes must be built on both banks to confine the water, only then can flooding be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: At high tide, however, Yellow River water backed up and stalled the flow. Upstream, over 200 li from the mouth to Xiangshui, channels split and rejoined unpredictably; only dikes on both banks could prevent flooding.

sentences.zh: 計工長三百餘裡，經費難籌。

translations.literal: Calculating works of more than 300 li in length, funds are difficult to raise.
translations.idiomatic: Works spanning more than 300 li would be prohibitively expensive.

sentences.zh: 且中河運道為黃流橫截，不得不移塘灌運。

translations.literal: Moreover the Middle River transport route is cut across by Yellow River flow, and it is unavoidable to shift transport from the Grand Canal to the Guan River route.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Grand Canal transport route would be cut by Yellow River water, forcing grain traffic onto the Guan River route.

sentences.zh: 清水本弱，仍恃借黃以濟。

translations.literal: Clear water is inherently weak and still relies on borrowing Yellow River water to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Clear water alone was too weak; transport still depended on Yellow River water to boost the current.

sentences.zh: 空船引轉需時，重運更形艱滯。

translations.literal: Turning empty boats requires time; heavy transport becomes even more difficult and obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: Turning empty barges would take longer, and laden convoys would face even greater delays.

sentences.zh: 是移塘乃權宜之計，常年行之，恐妨運道。

translations.literal: Thus shifting transport is an expedient measure; carrying it out year-round would likely obstruct the transport route.
translations.idiomatic: Shifting transport was a temporary expedient; making it permanent would likely cripple the grain route.

sentences.zh: 舊黃河自蕭莊迄舊海口四百二十餘裡，尾閭寬暢。

translations.literal: The old Yellow River from Xiaozhuang to the old estuary is more than 420 li, with a wide and open tail end.
translations.idiomatic: The old Yellow River channel from Xiaozhuang to the former estuary ran more than 420 li with a broad, open mouth.

sentences.zh: 自漫口斷流，河身益淤。

translations.literal: Since the overflow breach cut off flow, the river bed has become increasingly silted.
translations.idiomatic: Since the breach had cut off the flow, the riverbed had silted up further.

sentences.zh: 若挽歸故道，堵口挑河，共費五六百萬，較改河築堤撙節實多。

translations.literal: If diverting back to the old course, blocking the mouth and dredging the river, the total cost is five or six million, which in economy of expenditure is actually much more than changing the river course and building dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Returning the river to its old course—blocking the breach and dredging—would cost five or six million taels, far more than building dikes along the new channel.

sentences.zh: 請定明歲春融興工，俟軍船回空後築壩合龍。

translations.literal: Please fix next year when ice melts to begin work; after grain transport ships return empty, build the dam and close the dragon.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed beginning work the following spring after the ice thawed, closing the breach once the grain fleet had completed its northbound run.

sentences.zh: 」詔如議行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered implementation as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the plan carried out as proposed.

sentences.zh: 尋以戶部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was made Minister of Revenue and Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Minister of Revenue and Associate Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，偕侍郎何汝霖赴南河勘工，又赴河南察視中河廳漫口。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, together with Vice Minister He Rulin he went to the Southern Rivers to inspect works, and again went to Henan to examine the Middle River Bureau overflow breach.
translations.idiomatic: In 1843 he joined Vice Minister He Rulin to inspect Southern Rivers works and then went to Henan to survey the Middle River Bureau breach.

sentences.zh: 疏陳築壩挑河工費需銀五百十八萬兩，較祥符工費為節省，允之。

translations.literal: He memorialized that building the dam and dredging the river would require 5.18 million taels of silver, which compared with the Xiangfu project costs was economical; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that damming the breach and dredging the channel would cost 5.18 million taels—less than the Xiangfu project—and the plan was approved.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，奏：「河南下北河廳廟工，乃北岸七廳適中之所，河臣宜常年駐此，便於控制。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he memorialized: "The Miaogong works of the Henan Lower North River Bureau are the central point among the seven bureaus on the north bank; the river commissioner should reside here year-round for convenient control."
translations.idiomatic: In 1845 he argued that the Miaogong works of the Henan Lower North River Bureau lay at the center of the seven north-bank offices and that the river commissioner should be stationed there year-round for effective control.

sentences.zh: 」詔河督每於伏汛前移駐廟工，立冬後仍回濟寧。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the river commissioner to move his headquarters to Miaogong before the summer flood season each year, and after the Start of Winter still return to Jining.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the river commissioner to move to Miaogong before the summer flood season each year and return to Jining after winter began.

sentences.zh: 尋坐濫保駐藏大臣孟保，降內閣學士。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was punished for indiscriminately recommending Tibetan Resident Minister Meng Bao and was demoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon demoted to grand secretary for improperly recommending Tibetan resident minister Meng Bao.

sentences.zh: 未幾，复授工部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 又坐濫保科布多參贊大臣果勒明阿，褫職。

translations.literal: Again he was punished for indiscriminately recommending Kobdo Assistant Resident Minister Guoleming'a and was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of office again for improperly recommending Kobdo assistant resident minister Guoleming'a.

sentences.zh: 三十年，署正白旗滿洲副都統。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he served as Acting Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Manchu Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1850 he served as acting vice commander-in-chief of the Manchu Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，卒，詔念前勞，予一品銜，依尚書例賜卹，諡文★。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he died; an edict recalled his former labors, granted him first-rank insignia, bestowed condolence payments according to the precedent for ministers, and gave the posthumous title Wenke.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1851. The throne recalled his long service, granted him first-rank insignia and ministerial funeral honors, and gave him the posthumous title Wenke.

sentences.zh: 子恆恩，左副都御史；

translations.literal: His son Heng'en was Left Vice Censor-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: His son Heng'en became Left Vice Censor-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 孫盛昱，自有傳。

translations.literal: his grandson Shengyu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: his grandson Shengyu has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 宗室禧恩，字仲蕃，隸正藍旗，睿親王淳穎子。

translations.literal: Zongshi Xi'en, style name Zhongfan, was registered in the Plain Blue Banner, son of Prince Rui Chunying.
translations.idiomatic: Zongshi Xi'en, whose style name was Zhongfan, belonged to the Plain Blue Banner and was a son of Prince Rui Chunying.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年，賜頭品頂戴，授頭等侍衛，乾清門行走。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he was granted the first-rank insignia cap, appointed First Class Bodyguard, and allowed to attend at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.
translations.idiomatic: In 1801 he was granted the first-rank insignia cap, appointed a first-class bodyguard, and given attendance at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.

sentences.zh: 十年，晉御前侍衛，兼副都統、鑾儀使、上駟院卿，轉奉宸院卿，遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to Imperial Bodyguard, concurrently Vice Commander-in-Chief, Director of Imperial Processions, and Master of the Imperial Stud, then transferred to Master of the Imperial Parks, and moved to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1805 he was promoted to imperial bodyguard and concurrently served as vice commander-in-chief, director of imperial processions, and master of the imperial stud before becoming master of the imperial parks and grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢理籓院侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1813 he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授內務府大臣，調戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Minister of the Imperial Household and transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1815 he was appointed minister of the Imperial Household and transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，仁宗崩於熱河避暑山莊，事出倉猝，禧恩以內廷扈從，建議宣宗有定亂勳，當繼位。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Emperor Renzong died at the Rehe Mountain Resort; the matter arose in sudden haste. Xi'en, as an inner-court attendant on the journey, proposed that Emperor Xuanzong had merit in quelling disorder and ought to succeed to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jiaqing died suddenly at the Rehe resort in 1820, Xi'en, who was in the inner-court entourage, argued that the future Daoguang Emperor had earned merit in suppressing the Lin Qing rebellion and should succeed.

sentences.zh: 樞臣托津、戴均元等猶豫，禧恩抗論，眾不能奪。

translations.literal: Grand Councilors Tuojin, Dai Junyuan, and others hesitated; Xi'en argued forcefully, and the multitude could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand councilors Tuojin, Dai Junyuan, and others hesitated, but Xi'en argued forcefully and carried the day.

sentences.zh: 會得秘匱硃諭，乃偕諸臣奉宣宗即位，命在御前大臣、領侍衛大臣上行走。

translations.literal: Then they obtained the vermilion rescript from the secret casket and together with the various ministers installed Emperor Xuanzong on the throne; he was ordered to attend above the Imperial Presence Ministers and Chief Guard Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When the vermilion rescript was found in the secret casket, he joined the other ministers in installing the Daoguang Emperor and was ordered to attend above the ranks of imperial presence ministers and chief guard ministers.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，擢理籓院尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he was promoted to Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he was promoted to Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時哈薩克部眾潛聚烏梁海，議遷徙安置，增設卡倫。

translations.literal: At that time Kazakh tribesmen were secretly gathering at Wulianghai; it was discussed to relocate and settle them and increase guard posts.
translations.idiomatic: Kazakh tribesmen were then gathering secretly at Wulianghai, and officials debated resettling them and adding guard posts.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書松筠諳習邊事，上每垂詢，禧恩因以諮之。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Songyun was well versed in frontier affairs; the Emperor often made inquiries, and Xi'en therefore consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Songyun was expert in frontier affairs, and when the emperor consulted him, Xi'en sought his advice.

sentences.zh: 松筠素坦率，遂代刪改疏稿。

translations.literal: Songyun was by nature frank and forthright, and so on his behalf revised and edited the memorial draft.
translations.idiomatic: Songyun, who was habitually blunt, took it upon himself to revise Xi'en's memorial draft.

sentences.zh: 禧恩怒，以上聞，松筠坐越職干預被譴。

translations.literal: Xi'en was angry and reported it to the Emperor; Songyun was punished for overstepping his duties in interference.
translations.idiomatic: Xi'en was furious and reported the matter to the emperor; Songyun was rebuked for overstepping his authority.

sentences.zh: 尋調工部，仍兼署理籓院尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to the Ministry of Works, still concurrently serving as Acting Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of Works while continuing to act as minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1826 he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 八年，加太子少保，署吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and served as Acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1828 he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 九年，隨扈盛京，詔念睿親王多爾袞數定大勳，加恩後裔，賜禧恩雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he accompanied the imperial procession to Shengjing; an edict recalled that Prince Rui Dorgon several times established great merit, extended favor to his descendants, and granted Xi'en the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1829, on the imperial visit to Shengjing, an edict honored Prince Rui Dorgon's great services and granted Xi'en the double-eyed peacock feather as a descendant's privilege.

sentences.zh: 十二年，湖南江華瑤趙金龍作亂，命禧恩偕盛京將軍瑚松額督師，未至，總督盧坤、提督羅思舉已平之，殲金龍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Yao Zhao Jinlong of Jianghua in Hunan rebelled; Xi'en was ordered together with Shengjing Military Governor Husong'e to command the army. Before they arrived, Governor-General Lu Kun and Provincial Commander Luo Siju had already pacified it and destroyed Jinlong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1832, when the Yao leader Zhao Jinlong rebelled at Jianghua in Hunan, Xi'en was ordered to command the campaign with Shengjing Military Governor Husong'e—but before they arrived, Governor-General Lu Kun and Provincial Commander Luo Siju had already crushed the rebellion and killed Jinlong.

sentences.zh: 禧恩素貴倨，奉命視師，意氣甚盛，嗛諸將不待而告捷，謂金龍死未可信。

translations.literal: Xi'en had always been noble and arrogant; ordered to inspect the army, his spirit was very high. He resented that the generals reported victory without waiting for him and said Jinlong's death could not yet be believed.
translations.idiomatic: Xi'en, who had always been proud and overbearing, arrived in high spirits to take command. Resentful that the generals had reported victory without him, he declared that Jinlong's death could not yet be confirmed.

sentences.zh: 思舉以金龍焚骸及佩物為證，議始息。

translations.literal: Siju used Jinlong's burned remains and personal ornaments as proof, and the dispute then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Siju produced Jinlong's charred remains and personal effects as proof, and the dispute ended.

sentences.zh: 廣東瑤匪趙仔青竄入湖南，率提督餘步雲、總兵曾勝追剿之；

translations.literal: The Yao bandit Zhao Zaiqing of Guangdong fled into Hunan; he led Provincial Commander Yu Buyun and Major General Zeng Sheng in pursuit and suppression;
translations.idiomatic: When the Yao bandit Zhao Zaiqing fled from Guangdong into Hunan, he led Provincial Commander Yu Buyun and Major General Zeng Sheng in pursuit;

sentences.zh: 偕巡撫吳榮光疏陳善後事。

translations.literal: together with Governor Wu Rongguang he memorialized on matters of post-pacification.
translations.idiomatic: and together with Governor Wu Rongguang memorialized on post-pacification measures.

sentences.zh: 湖南既定，而兩廣總督李鴻賓剿連山瑤，閱半年，軍屢挫。

translations.literal: Hunan was already settled, but Liangguang Governor-General Li Hongbin was suppressing the Lianshan Yao; after half a year the army suffered repeated setbacks.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hunan was pacified, Liangguang Governor-General Li Hongbin was still fighting the Lianshan Yao, and after six months his forces had suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 詔逮鴻賓，以禧恩署總督，由湖南進兵。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Li Hongbin arrested; Xi'en was made Acting Governor-General and advanced the army from Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongbin was arrested, Xi'en was made acting governor-general, and troops advanced from Hunan.

sentences.zh: 遣步雲、勝等先後破賊，擒首逆鄧三、盤文理，毀其巢。

translations.literal: He sent Buyun, Sheng, and others in succession to defeat the bandits, captured the chief rebels Deng San and Pan Wenli, and destroyed their lairs.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yu Buyun, Zeng Sheng, and others to defeat the rebels in succession, capturing the ringleaders Deng San and Pan Wenli and destroying their strongholds.

sentences.zh: 甫一月，諸瑤乞降。

translations.literal: After only one month, the various Yao groups begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the Yao groups were suing for peace.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其奏功迅速，賜三眼花翎，封不入八分輔國公。

translations.literal: An edict praised his rapid report of achievement, granted the triple-eyed peacock feather, and enfeoffed him as Duke Who Assists the State without the eight shares reduction.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised his swift success, granted him the triple-eyed peacock feather, and enfeoffed him as Duke Who Assists the State without income reduction.

sentences.zh: 班師，途次丁母憂，溫諭慰之。

translations.literal: On returning from campaign, en route he entered mourning for his mother; a warm edict comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home he received news of his mother's death; the emperor sent a warm message of condolence.

sentences.zh: 十三年，孝慎皇后薨，命理喪儀，坐議禮徵引違制，褫御前大臣、戶部尚書、內務府大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Empress Xiaoshen died; he was charged with arranging funeral rites and was punished because in deliberating ritual citations he violated regulations, stripped of Imperial Presence Minister, Minister of Revenue, and Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In 1833, when Empress Xiaoshen died, he was put in charge of the funeral rites but was dismissed as imperial presence minister, minister of revenue, and minister of the Imperial Household for citing ritual precedents that violated regulations.

sentences.zh: 尋复授理籓院尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was again appointed Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以生日受屬員饋送，為御史趙敦詩所劾，疏辯得直，敦詩坐譴。

translations.literal: Because on his birthday he received gifts from subordinate officials, he was impeached by Censor Zhao Dunshi; in his memorial in defense he was vindicated, and Dunshi was punished.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Zhao Dunshi impeached him for accepting birthday gifts from subordinates, his defense was accepted and Zhao Dunshi was punished instead.

sentences.zh: 十四年，因相度龍泉峪萬年吉地，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, because of surveying the auspicious site for ten thousand years at Longquan Valley, he was given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1834 he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent for surveying the imperial mausoleum site at Longquan Valley.

sentences.zh: 調兵部尚書，兼署禮部戶部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of War, concurrently acting for the Ministries of Rites and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of War and concurrently acted for the Ministries of Rites and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十八年，詔以南苑牲畜不蕃，禧恩久管奉宸苑，廢弛疏懈，罷其兼領。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year an edict said that because livestock in the Southern Park were not multiplying, and Xi'en had long managed the Imperial Parks and been negligent and lax, his concurrent posts were removed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 an edict blamed the decline of livestock in the Southern Park on Xi'en's long mismanagement of the Imperial Parks and stripped him of his concurrent posts.

sentences.zh: 尋得員司積弊狀，盡罷諸兼職，降內閣學士。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward evidence of accumulated abuses by staff officials was obtained; all his concurrent posts were removed and he was demoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When evidence of long-standing abuses by his staff emerged, all his concurrent posts were removed and he was demoted to grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，署盛京將軍，授理籓院侍郎，留將軍署任。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he served as Acting Military Governor of Shengjing, was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs, and retained the acting military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In 1842 he served as acting Military Governor of Shengjing, was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs, and retained the acting governorship.

sentences.zh: 英吉利內犯，海疆戒嚴，命治盛京防務。

translations.literal: England invaded inland; the coastal frontiers were placed on alert, and he was ordered to manage Shengjing frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Britain invaded and the coast was placed on alert, he was ordered to organize Shengjing's defenses.

sentences.zh: 既而和議成，疏陳善後十事，並巡洋章程，如議行。

translations.literal: Afterward peace negotiations were concluded; he memorialized ten matters for post-settlement and regulations for coastal patrol, all implemented as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was concluded, he memorialized ten post-war measures and coastal patrol regulations, which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以病解職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he resigned office due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1845 he resigned due to illness.

sentences.zh: 坐失察內地民人越朝鮮界墾地，削公爵，降二等輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He was punished for failure to detect inland civilians crossing the Korean border to open land for cultivation; his ducal title was removed and he was demoted to Second Rank Assistant General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of his ducal title and demoted to assistant general for failing to stop civilians from farming across the Korean border.

sentences.zh: 三十年，起署馬蘭鎮總兵、密雲副都統。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was recalled to serve as Acting Major General of Malan Garrison and Vice Commander-in-Chief of Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: In 1850 he was recalled to serve as acting commander of Malan Garrison and vice commander-in-chief of Miyun.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，召授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二年，擢戶部尚書，協辦大學士，管理籓院事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to Minister of Revenue, Associate Grand Secretary, and charged with managing Court of Colonial Affairs affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he was promoted to Minister of Revenue and Associate Grand Secretary and put in charge of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太子太保，諡文莊。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died; he was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous title Wenzuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the title Wenzuang.

sentences.zh: 禧恩自道光初被恩眷，及孝全皇后被選入宮，家故寒素，賴其資助，遂益用事。

translations.literal: From the beginning of Daoguang Xi'en received imperial favor; when Empress Xiaoquan was selected to enter the palace, her family was originally poor and plain and relied on his financial support, and he therefore wielded power ever more.
translations.idiomatic: Xi'en had enjoyed imperial favor since the early Daoguang years. When Empress Xiaoquan entered the palace, her impoverished family relied on his support, and his influence grew accordingly.

sentences.zh: 遍膺禁近要職，兼攝諸部，凌轢同列，人皆側目。

translations.literal: He broadly received important posts close to the Forbidden precincts, concurrently held various ministries, bullied his colleagues, and everyone looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: He held one key inner-court post after another, concurrently headed multiple ministries, bullied his colleagues, and drew widespread resentment.

sentences.zh: 後晚寵衰，禧恩亦數獲譴罷斥。

translations.literal: Later when evening favor declined, Xi'en also several times received reprimands and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress's influence waned in her later years, Xi'en was repeatedly reprimanded and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，乃復起，不兩年登協揆焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, he was then restored; within less than two years he rose to associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianfeng ascended the throne, he was restored and within two years reached the associate grand secretary rank.

sentences.zh: 陳官俊，字偉堂，山東濰縣人。

translations.literal: Chen Guanjun, style name Weitang, was a native of Weixian in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guanjun, whose style name was Weitang, was a native of Weixian in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷贊善。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, appointed Compiler, and moved to Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations as a jinshi in 1808, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, was appointed a compiler, and was promoted to tutor.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，入直上書房。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he entered the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In 1816 he joined the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 大考二等，擢洗馬，累遷右庶子。

translations.literal: In the grand examination he ranked second class, was promoted to Keeper of the Heir Apparent's Stables, and rose in succession to Right Vice Director of Studies.
translations.idiomatic: After ranking second class in the palace examination, he was promoted to Keeper of the Heir Apparent's Stables and rose to Right Vice Director of Studies.

sentences.zh: 典陝西鄉試，督山西學政。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shaanxi provincial examination and supervised as Educational Commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Shaanxi provincial examinations and served as educational commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，命各省明定陋規，中外臣工多言窒礙，官俊亦疏陳不可行，詔嘉之，予議敘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang an order was issued for each province clearly to define improper customary fees; Chinese and foreign officials many said it would cause obstruction, and Guanjun also memorialized that it could not be carried out. An edict praised this and granted him consideration for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821, when the throne ordered provinces to abolish improper customary fees, many officials objected that the policy would be unworkable. Guanjun agreed in a memorial, won the emperor's praise, and received consideration for promotion.

sentences.zh: 會密諭留心察訪官吏賢否、政治得失，官俊恃曾直內廷為宣宗所眷，意氣甚張。

translations.literal: Then a secret edict ordered careful investigation of whether officials were worthy and of political gains and losses; Guanjun relied on having once served directly in the inner court and being favored by Emperor Xuanzong, and his spirit was very overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: When a secret edict ordered officials to report on local governance, Guanjun, confident in his former inner-court service and the Daoguang Emperor's favor, became increasingly overbearing.

sentences.zh: 尋遷侍講學士，命回京，仍直上書房。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was moved to Reader of the Hanlin Academy, ordered to return to the capital, and still served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Hanlin reader, recalled to Beijing, and returned to the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 山西巡撫成格追劾官俊在學政任毆差買妾，妄作威福，大開奔競。

translations.literal: Shanxi Governor Cheng'e pursued impeachment of Guanjun for during his term as educational commissioner beating runners, buying concubines, presumptuously wielding power and favor, and greatly opening the door to factional competition.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi Governor Cheng'e impeached him for beating runners, buying concubines, abusing his authority, and encouraging corrupt patronage during his term as educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上以官俊於毆差買妾已自承不諱，曾薦舉魏元烺、邱鳴泰，人材尚不繆；

translations.literal: The Emperor considered that Guanjun regarding beating runners and buying concubines had himself confessed without concealment, and that he had once recommended Wei Yuanhuang and Qiu Mingtai—his judgment of talent was still not wrong;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted that Guanjun had confessed to beating runners and buying concubines, and that his recommendations of Wei Yuanhuang and Qiu Mingtai showed his judgment of talent was not wholly mistaken;

sentences.zh: 惟所述太監往河東查訪鹽務控案，事出無稽，解職就質，命長齡道出山西，傳旨面詰成格，亦以不能指實引咎，遂兩斥之。

translations.literal: only the account of eunuchs going to Hedong to investigate salt administration accusation cases was groundless. He was removed from office to face questioning; Changling was ordered to pass through Shanxi en route and transmit an edict to question Cheng'e in person. Cheng'e also could not substantiate his charges and took blame; thus both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: but Cheng'e's claim that eunuchs had been sent to Hedong to investigate salt affairs was unfounded. Guanjun was dismissed pending investigation; Changling was ordered to question Cheng'e in Shanxi en route. When Cheng'e could not substantiate his charges, both men were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 官俊降編修，罷直上書房。

translations.literal: Guanjun was demoted to Compiler and removed from the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: Guanjun was demoted to compiler and removed from the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 連典貴州、江西鄉試，歷中允、祭酒、侍講學士、內閣學士。

translations.literal: In succession he presided over the Guizhou and Jiangxi provincial examinations, served as Middle Supervisor, Libationer, Reader of the Hanlin Academy, and Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Guizhou and Jiangxi provincial examinations in succession and rose through middle supervisor, libationer, Hanlin reader, and grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 十六年，授禮部侍郎，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1836 he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十九年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1839 he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 東陵郎中慶玉侵帑籍沒，主事全孚預告，多所寄頓。

translations.literal: Eastern Mausoleum Bureau Director Qingyu embezzled treasury funds and was confiscated; Principal Secretary Quanfu had given advance warning and had many deposits entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Mausoleum Bureau Director Qingyu was convicted of embezzlement, Principal Secretary Quanfu, who had warned him in advance, was found to hold many deposits on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 事覺，語由官俊閒談漏洩，回奏复諱飾，詔斥失大臣體，褫職。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, the information had leaked through Guanjun's casual conversation; in his memorial reply he again concealed and glossed over it. An edict rebuked him for losing a grand minister's dignity and stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: The leak was traced to casual remarks by Guanjun, and when he reported back he tried to cover it up. An edict denounced his conduct as unworthy of a senior minister and stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，起為通政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was restored as Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In 1841 he was restored as commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部、吏部侍郎，管理三庫。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Minister of Revenue and Personnel and managed the Three Treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of revenue and personnel and managed the Three Treasuries.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部尚書，調工部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以吏部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was made Minister of Personnel and Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1844 he was made Minister of Personnel and Associate Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 官俊再起，歷典鄉會試、殿廷禦試，每與衡校。

translations.literal: Guanjun was restored again, presided in succession over provincial and metropolitan examinations and palace imperial examinations, each time participating in grading.
translations.idiomatic: After his restoration, Guanjun repeatedly presided over provincial, metropolitan, and palace examinations as a chief examiner.

sentences.zh: 充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: He served as Chief Tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 編修童福承素無行，直上書房授皇子讀。

translations.literal: Compiler Tong Fucheng had always been without proper conduct yet taught princes in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Tong Fucheng, who had a poor reputation, was nevertheless assigned to teach princes in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳壇劾之，語及福承為官俊妻作祭文，措詞過當。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Chen Tan impeached him, mentioning that Fucheng had written a funeral elegy for Guanjun's wife with excessively ornate wording.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Chen Tan impeached him, citing among other things an overly ornate funeral elegy Tong Fucheng had written for Guanjun's wife.

sentences.zh: 福承譴黜，詔斥官俊容隱不奏，罷總師傅，議降三級調用，從寬留任。

translations.literal: Fucheng was reprimanded and dismissed; an edict rebuked Guanjun for concealing and not reporting it, removed him as Chief Tutor, deliberated demotion three ranks and transfer, but leniently allowed him to retain his post.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Fucheng was dismissed. An edict rebuked Guanjun for concealing the matter, stripped him of the chief tutorship, and considered demoting him three ranks—but leniently allowed him to keep his post.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，卒，優詔賜卹，稱其心田坦白，贈太子太保，入祀賢良祠，諡文愨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died; a favorable edict granted condolence payments, praised his open and candid mind, posthumously gave Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, entered worship in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, posthumous title Wenque.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1849. A gracious edict granted funeral honors, praised his open character, made him posthumous Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and gave him the posthumous title Wenque.

sentences.zh: 賜其孫厚鍾、厚滋並為舉人。

translations.literal: His grandsons Houzhong and Houzi were both granted the status of provincial graduates.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons Houzhong and Houzi were both granted provincial graduate status.

sentences.zh: 官俊初直上書房，授宣宗長子奕緯讀，宣宗嘉其訓迪有方。

translations.literal: When Guanjun first served in the Southern Study, he taught Emperor Xuanzong's eldest son Yizhi; Emperor Xuanzong praised his instruction and guidance as well directed.
translations.idiomatic: Guanjun's first posting in the Southern Study was tutoring the Daoguang Emperor's eldest son Yizhi, whom the emperor praised him for instructing well.

sentences.zh: 後皇長子逾冠而薨，上深以為恫，故遇官俊特厚，屢獲咎而恩禮始終不衰。

translations.literal: Later the eldest imperial son passed the capping age and died; the Emperor was deeply grieved, and therefore treated Guanjun especially generously. Though he repeatedly incurred blame, favor and courtesy never declined to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When the eldest prince died shortly after coming of age, the grieving emperor treated Guanjun with special favor that never waned despite his repeated disgraces.

sentences.zh: 子介祺，道光二十五年進士，官編修。

translations.literal: His son Jieqi was a jinshi in the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang and served as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jieqi passed the examinations as a jinshi in 1845 and served as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，助軍餉，加侍講學士銜。

translations.literal: During Xianfeng he contributed military funds and was given the rank of Reader of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng reign he contributed military funds and was given the rank of Hanlin reader.

sentences.zh: 後在籍治團練，守城，賑饑，賜二品頂戴。

translations.literal: Later while at home he organized militia training, defended the city, relieved famine, and was granted the second-rank insignia cap.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while at home, he organized militia, defended the city, and relieved famine victims, for which he was granted the second-rank insignia cap.

sentences.zh: 介祺績學好古，所藏鐘鼎、彝器、金石為近代之冠。

translations.literal: Jieqi was accomplished in learning and fond of antiquity; his collection of bells, cauldrons, ritual vessels, and metal and stone inscriptions was the finest of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Jieqi was a distinguished scholar-antiquarian whose collection of bronzes and epigraphic stones was unrivaled in his day.

sentences.zh: 卓秉恬，字靜遠，四川華陽人。

translations.literal: Zhuo Bingtian, style name Jingyuan, was a native of Huayang in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Bingtian, whose style name was Jingyuan, was a native of Huayang in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年進士，選庶吉士，年甫逾冠，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, had just passed the capping age, and was appointed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations as a jinshi in 1802, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor while still in his early twenties, and was appointed a reviser.

sentences.zh: 典陝西鄉試。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shaanxi provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Shaanxi provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 十八年，改御史，歷給事中，章疏凡數十上。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Censor, served successively as Supervising Secretary, and memorialized several tens of times.
translations.idiomatic: In 1813 he was made a censor, rose to supervising secretary, and submitted dozens of memorials.

sentences.zh: 論盜風未息，由捕役與盜賊因緣為奸，捕役藉盜賊以漁利，盜賊仗捕役為護符，民間控告，官不為理，盜賊結恨，又召荼毒；

translations.literal: He discussed that banditry had not ceased because constables and bandits formed connections to do evil together—constables relied on bandits to fish for profit, bandits relied on constables as protective talismans; when civilians lodged accusations officials did not act, bandits harbored resentment and again brought calamity;
translations.idiomatic: He argued that banditry persisted because constables colluded with thieves—constables profited from protecting criminals, and criminals used constables as shields. When civilians complained, officials ignored them, breeding resentment and further violence;

sentences.zh: 直隸之大名、滄州，河南之衛輝、陳州、山東之曹州、東昌、武定，江甦之徐州最甚，請飭實力禁懲。

translations.literal: in Zhili at Daming and Cangzhou, in Henan at Weihui and Chenzhou, in Shandong at Caozhou, Dongchang, and Wuding, and in Jiangsu at Xuzhou it was most severe—please order strict prohibition and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: with the worst abuses in Daming and Cangzhou in Zhili, Weihui and Chenzhou in Henan, Caozhou, Dongchang, and Wuding in Shandong, and Xuzhou in Jiangsu. He urged strict enforcement.

sentences.zh: 巡漕山東，履勘泰安、兗州各屬，探濬新泉四十三處，定名勒石。

translations.literal: On grain transport inspection in Shandong, he personally surveyed Tai'an, Yanzhou, and their subordinates, explored and dredged forty-three new springs, fixed names and carved them on stone.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting grain transport in Shandong, he surveyed Tai'an, Yanzhou, and neighboring districts, opened forty-three new springs, and had their names inscribed on stone markers.

sentences.zh: 歷鴻臚寺少卿、順天府丞。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice President of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Assistant Magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice president of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and assistant magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，疏言：「由陝西略陽迄東至湖北鄖西，謂之南山老林；

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he memorialized, saying: "From Lueyang in Shaanxi eastward to Yunxi in Hubei is called the old forest of the Southern Mountains;
translations.idiomatic: In 1825 he memorialized that the tract from Lueyang in Shaanxi east to Yunxi in Hubei was known as the Southern Mountains old forest;

sentences.zh: 由陝西寧羌迄南而東，經四川境至湖北保康，謂之巴山老林。

translations.literal: from Ningqiang in Shaanxi south and east, passing through Sichuan territory to Baokang in Hubei, is called the old forest of the Ba Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: and from Ningqiang south and east through Sichuan to Baokang in Hubei as the Ba Mountains old forest.

sentences.zh: 地皆磽瘠，糧徭極微。

translations.literal: The land is all barren and poor; grain levies and corvée are extremely slight.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was barren and grain taxes and corvée were negligible.

sentences.zh: 無業遊民，給地主錢數千，即租種數溝數嶺。

translations.literal: Unemployed vagrants give landlords several thousand cash and then rent-cultivate several ravines and several ridges.
translations.idiomatic: Landless migrants paid landlords a few thousand cash to farm a ravine or hillside.

sentences.zh: 歲薄不收則徙去，謂之棚民。

translations.literal: In years of poor harvest they move away; they are called shed people.
translations.idiomatic: They moved on when harvests failed and were known as shed people.

sentences.zh: 良莠莫辨，攘奪時聞。

translations.literal: Good and bad cannot be distinguished; plunder and seizure are heard of from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Good and bad were indistinguishable, and robbery was common.

sentences.zh: 一遇旱澇，一二奸民為之倡，即蟻附蜂起。

translations.literal: Whenever drought or flood occurs, one or two wicked civilians take the lead and they swarm like ants and rise like bees.
translations.idiomatic: In drought or flood, a few ringleaders could draw crowds that swarmed like ants.

sentences.zh: 州縣以地方遼闊，莫能追捕，遂至互相容隱。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties, because the territory is vast, cannot pursue and capture them, and thus come to mutual concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials, unable to police such vast territory, often concealed the problem instead.

sentences.zh: 迨釀成大案，即加參劾，事已無濟。

translations.literal: Only when a major case is brewed do they add impeachment, but the matter is already beyond remedy.
translations.idiomatic: By the time a major case erupted and officials were impeached, it was too late.

sentences.zh: 且事連三省，大吏往返諮商，州縣奉文辦理，恆在數月之後。

translations.literal: Moreover the matter involves three provinces; high officials go back and forth in consultation, and prefectures and counties receive documents to handle affairs, always months later.
translations.idiomatic: Because the region spanned three provinces, high officials exchanged messages while local governments acted months after orders arrived.

sentences.zh: 與其即一隅而專謀之，何如合三省而共議之。

translations.literal: Rather than planning for one corner alone, how much better to unite the three provinces and deliberate together.
translations.idiomatic: Rather than addressing each corner separately, he proposed joint deliberation across all three provinces.

sentences.zh: 請於扼要之地，專設大員控制。

translations.literal: Please at strategic points specially establish a high official to control affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that a senior official be posted at a strategic point to oversee the region.

sentences.zh: 」宣宗深韙之，詔下三省會議，未果行，僅將邊境文武酌就要地改駐添設。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong deeply approved it and ordered the three provinces to confer; it was not ultimately carried out, and only the civil and military officials on the frontier were weighed for relocation and additional posts at key points.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoguang Emperor strongly approved and ordered the three provinces to confer, but the plan was never fully implemented—only some frontier posts were relocated or added.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，調奉天府丞，丁父憂去。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang he was transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture and left office on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In 1824 he was transferred to assistant magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture and left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，歷太僕寺、大理寺少卿，太僕寺卿，宗人府丞，內閣學士，典江南鄉試。
