translations.literal: When mourning ended he served successively as Vice President of the Court of the Imperial Stud and Court of Judicial Review, President of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he rose through vice president of the Court of the Imperial Stud and Court of Judicial Review, president of the Court of the Imperial Stud, vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, and grand secretary, and presided over the Jiangnan provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷禮部侍郎，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was moved to Vice Minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he was made Vice Minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 督浙江學政。

translations.literal: He supervised as Educational Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as educational commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 擢左都御史，召還京，兼管順天府尹事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, summoned back to the capital, and concurrently managed affairs of the Shuntian Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, recalled to Beijing, and put in charge of Shuntian Prefecture affairs.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部、戶部、吏部尚書、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: He served successively as Minister of War, Revenue, and Personnel, and Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He served as minister of war, revenue, and personnel and as associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，拜文淵閣大學士，晉武英殿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and advanced to the Hall of Military Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: In 1844 he was made Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and promoted to the Hall of Military Eminence.

sentences.zh: 歷管兵部、戶部、工部，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He successively managed the Ministries of War, Revenue, and Works and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He headed the Ministries of War, Revenue, and Works in turn and was granted the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，卒，年七十四，贈太子太保，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng he died, age seventy-four; he was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1855 at the age of seventy-four and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the title Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 秉恬兼管京尹最久，凡十有八年。

translations.literal: Bingtian concurrently managed the capital magistracy the longest, altogether eighteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtian held concurrent charge of the capital magistracy longer than anyone else—a total of eighteen years.

sentences.zh: 時九卿會議，一二王公樞相主之，餘率佔位畫諾。

translations.literal: At that time in conferences of the Nine Ministers, one or two princes and grand councilors presided, and the rest generally occupied seats and marked approval.
translations.idiomatic: At Nine Ministers' conferences, one or two princes or grand councilors dominated while the rest merely nodded assent.

sentences.zh: 秉恬在列，時有辯論，不為用事者所喜。

translations.literal: Bingtian was among them and from time to time debated; he was not liked by those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtian often spoke up in debate, which won him no favor among those in power.

sentences.zh: 子枟，道光二十年進士，官至吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Ting was a jinshi in the twentieth year of Daoguang and rose to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ting passed the examinations as a jinshi in 1840 and rose to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自設軍機處，閣臣不預樞務。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Since the establishment of the Grand Council, grand secretaries do not participate in confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: After the Grand Council was established, grand secretaries no longer took part in confidential state affairs.

sentences.zh: 始猶取名德較著者表望中朝，繼則旅進旅退之流，且以年資眷睞，馴躋鼎鉉矣。

translations.literal: At first men of rather notable reputation and virtue were still chosen to display prestige at court; later came the sort who advance and retire in company, and through seniority and imperial favor smoothly ascended to the highest ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: At first men of real reputation still lent the court dignity; later, mediocrities advanced by seniority and favor until they reached the highest office with scarcely a ripple.

sentences.zh: 寶興號嫺吏事，而蒙簠簋不飭之聲；

translations.literal: Baoxing was said to be skilled in administrative affairs, yet bore the reputation of not keeping his ritual vessels in order;
translations.idiomatic: Baoxing was considered capable in administration yet bore a reputation for personal impropriety;

sentences.zh: 敬徵數視河工，差著勞勚；

translations.literal: Jingzheng several times inspected river works and showed some merit in labor;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzheng inspected river works repeatedly and earned some credit for his efforts;

sentences.zh: 禧恩、陳官俊並恃恩私，崛而復起；

translations.literal: Xi'en and Chen Guanjun both relied on private favor, rose again after falling;
translations.idiomatic: Xi'en and Chen Guanjun both relied on private favor to rise again after falling;

sentences.zh: 卓秉恬以言官進，視緘默自安者稍表異焉。

translations.literal: Zhuo Bingtian advanced through censorial office and, compared with those who keep silent and rest content, showed himself somewhat different.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Bingtian rose through the censorate and stood out slightly from officials who kept silent and looked only to their own comfort.
